newsitem.title: USA: Roche drug approved by U.S. FDA.
newsitem.headline: Roche drug approved by U.S. FDA.

text.p: Hoffmann-LaRoche Inc has received approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to market FEMSTAT One, a drug for vulvovaginal infections, KV Pharmaceutical Co said Thursday.
KV said it would produce the drug, whose active ingredient is butoconazole nitrate, under an agreement with Roche Holding Ltd. Hoffman-La Roche is part of the Roche group.
FEMSTAT One, "a one day, one dose cure" for the infection caused by Candida albicans, uses KV's site release technology, KV said.
It said it will receive manufacturing and royalty revenues on the sale of the drug in North America, as well as semi-exclusive marketing rights in the region.
It will also get exclusive marketing and licensing rights for the rest of the world, it said.
KV said the market for such vaginal anti-fungal prescriptions in the United States was estimated at $150 million.
